question: What is the primary purpose of using supportive devices like pillows and trochanter rolls?

options.A: To prevent the patient from speaking
options.D: To speed up intravenous infusion rates

explanation: Supportive devices keep joints in a natural, neutral position to prevent deformities like footdrop and muscle strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is proper body alignment especially critical for an immobile patient?

options.A: Bones become completely rigid and cannot be moved after one hour
options.B: Immobile patients require less blood flow to their limbs
options.C: Natural body weight causes joints to twist into abnormal postures without support
options.D: Immobile patients cannot feel pain in their joints

explanation: Without active movement, gravity pulls limbs into awkward positions that can hurt joints and nerves. Pillows and rolls are your best friends here! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: How is a patient positioned when they are in the supine position?

options.B: On their side with top knee flexed

explanation: The supine position means lying horizontally on the back, facing upward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient recovering from spinal surgery needs to lie flat on their abdomen to allow full extension of their hip joints. Which position should you use?
explanation: Think of prone as lying face down on your tummy! It's great for straightening out those hip and knee joints. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which position is most commonly used when giving an adult patient an enema?
explanation: Sims is a side-lying position with the top leg bent. It gives you a safe, clear view and easy access to the rectum. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of placing a patient in the lateral (side-lying) position?

options.A: It maximizes lung expansion for asthma attacks
options.B: It takes weight off the sacrum and heels
options.C: It allows the patient to eat solid food safely
options.D: It provides direct access for urinary catheter insertion

explanation: Rolling a patient onto their side takes heavy pressure off the tailbone and heels, keeping their skin safe from bedsores! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the bed elevation angle for a patient in the semi-Fowler's position?
explanation: Semi-Fowler's raises the head of the bed moderately, usually between 30 and 45 degrees, to aid breathing. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: A patient with heart failure suddenly feels short of breath. Which nursing action should you take first regarding their position?

options.A: Place the patient face down in the prone position
options.B: Elevate the head of the bed to semi-Fowler's
options.C: Tilt the bed head downward into Trendelenburg
options.D: Lay the patient completely flat in the supine position

explanation: Sitting them up in semi-Fowler's makes breathing so much easier by taking pressure off their lungs and heart. Great job! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: How is the bed arranged when a patient is placed in the Trendelenburg position?

options.A: Head is higher than the feet
options.B: Knees are bent and flat on the mattress
options.C: Head is lower than the feet
options.D: Bed is bent in the middle like a folding chair

explanation: In Trendelenburg, the whole bed tilts so the patient's head is lower than their feet. Gravity helps blood flow to the brain! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which clinical situation is best suited for the reverse Trendelenburg position (head higher than feet)?

options.B: Treating sudden low blood pressure after trauma
options.C: Preventing severe acid reflux in a patient with a hiatal hernia
options.D: Placing a central venous line in the neck

explanation: Reverse Trendelenburg tilts the bed so the head is up, using gravity to keep stomach acid down where it belongs. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: During which procedure is the lithotomy position most commonly used?

options.B: Listening to breath sounds in asthma

explanation: Lithotomy has the patient on their back with feet up in stirrups, perfect for pelvic checks and welcoming new babies! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is a major safety rule nurses must follow when a patient is in the lithotomy position?

options.A: Turning the patient every thirty minutes without fail
options.B: Padding the stirrups to protect nerves and blood vessels
options.C: Keeping the head of the bed elevated to 90 degrees
options.D: Removing all pillows from beneath the patient's head

explanation: Bare metal stirrups can pinch nerves and block blood flow in the legs. Always make sure those stirrups are well-padded! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: How often should you turn an immobile patient to protect their skin from pressure sores?
explanation: Turning patients every two hours lets blood flow back into pressed skin, stopping pressure injuries before they start. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: Which nursing action prevents skin damage (shear forces) when moving a patient up in bed?

options.A: Using a draw sheet to lift the patient slightly off the mattress
options.B: Applying heavy lotion to the patient's heels and sacrum
options.C: Pulling the patient quickly by their ankles across the sheets
options.D: Lowering the head of the bed completely flat before moving

explanation: Always lift, never drag! A draw sheet prevents friction that can tear delicate skin layers against the bed sheet. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: Which detail do you NOT need to write down when documenting a patient position change?

options.A: The exact time the repositioning took place
options.B: The condition of the skin during the turn
options.C: The brand name of the hospital mattress
options.D: The specific position the patient was placed in

explanation: Mattress brands don't affect clinical care notes. Just focus on the position, skin condition, and exact time! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h8)

question: What should you do if a confused patient repeatedly refuses to be turned to their side?

options.A: Tell the patient they will be discharged if they do not comply
options.B: Document the refusal, explain the risks, and notify the primary nurse or provider
options.C: Document that the patient is sleeping and skip all future turns
options.D: Ignore the refusal and hold the patient down forcibly

explanation: Patients have a right to refuse, but as their nurse, you must gently educate them on the risks and report it properly. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h8)
